name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  March 7, 2011

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, Housing Authority, and the Library Board of Trustees of the
City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Leckness at 5:01 p.m., on March
7, 2011, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on March 4, 2011, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Kelley (arrived at 5:07 p.m.)
  Council Member Reardon
  Council Member Schlicht (arrived at 5:04 p.m.)
  Mayor Pro Tem Ury
  Mayor Leckness

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Irwin B. Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Leckness

INVOCATION: Mayor Leckness

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Labor Negotiations—The City Council will Provide Direction to its Labor
  Negotiator Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6. The Parties to the

City Council Minutes  1  March 7, 2011
   Negotiations are the City and the City's Unrepresented Employees. The City's
  Negotiator is Dennis Wilberg.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:02 p.m., Mayor Leckness recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:03 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the City Council received updates and information on
personnel matters but there was no reportable action from Closed Session.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Adoptable Pets of the Month

  Mayor Leckness highlighted three animals available for adoption at the Mission Viejo
  Animal Services Center.

P2.  Presentation of Award by Vocational Visions to the City of Mission Viejo as
  "Employer of the Year"

  Mayor Leckness received the presentation from Ed Kenna, Chairman of the Board, and
  Kathryn Hebel, Executive Director of Vocational Visions.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Ross Chun, Aliso Viejo: extended an invitation to the 2011 Sustainability Forum on March 31 in
Aliso Viejo.

Karen Gee, Anaheim: introduced a new countywide arts education program called the Trash
Artist Challenge. Residents can visit http://trashartist.com for more information.

Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: thanked the city for posting a blog article regarding the Regional
Chamber of Commerce nominations for outstanding businesses and business leaders. She
encouraged business owners to nominate themselves or others for outstanding work in the
community.

Harry Lenczyk (via email), M.V.: Mayor Leckness read an email from Mr. Lenczyk who
supports maintenance of the present population and who is opposed to new apartments in
Mission Viejo.

City Council Minutes  2  March 7, 2011
 CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 7, 8, 9, and 10 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said
  titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title
  and further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the Regular City Council Meeting of February 21, 2011, as
  presented.

3.  Summary of Fiscal Year 2010 - 2011 Budget Amendments to Date

  Received report.

4.  Check Register dated February 11, 2011, in the amount of $724,434.99

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Check Register dated February 18, 2011, in the amount of $409,498.73

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  Audit Report for the Air Quality Improvement Fund For The Fiscal Year Ended
  June 30, 2010 and AB 2766 Annual Program Report, FY 2009-10

  Received and filed.

11.  Damages Related to the Winter Storms of 2010

City Council Minutes  3  March 7, 2011
   (1) Approved the First Amendment to LT Engineering in an amount not to exceed
  $370,000 for the Annual Maintenance Program for the Repair and Reconstruction of
  Streets, Drainage Channels, Storm Drains, Slopes, and Emergency Services Contract for
  costs associated with the 2010 winter storms; (2) approved the Sixth Amendment to West
  Coast Arborists, Inc. in an amount not to exceed $65,000 for the Annual Routine Tree
  Trimming Contract for costs associated with the 2010 winter storms; and (3) adopted
  Resolution 11-18 Amending the Fiscal Year 2010-2011 Budget for Expenses Related to
  the December 2010 Winter Storms.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

OLD BUSINESS

12.  Olympiad Road Finish Line (CIP 781) and Ziggy the Bear Project - Budget and
  Schedule for Completion of CIP 781

  Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  Council Members Schlicht and Reardon expressed their preference to postpone
  consideration of this project until the budgeting process is underway.

  Motion made by Mayor Leckness, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to (1) receive
  and file the estimate of probable construction cost and schedule for the Olympiad Road
  Finish Line; and (2) direct staff to proceed with the construction and completion of CIP
  781; and (3) adopt Resolution 11-19 Amending the Fiscal Year 2010-2011 Budget for
  the Olympiad Road Finish Line (CIP 781) and Ziggy the Bear Project.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, and Ury
  NOES:  Reardon and Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

NEW BUSINESS

13.  Presentation by Michael Battaglia of Standard Pacific Homes Regarding Their
  Interest in Annexing into the City of Mission Viejo Approximately 38.4 Acres of
  Undeveloped Land Along the South Side of El Toro Road, Adjacent to and
  Northerly of the Painted Trails Residential Community for Future Single Family
  Home Development

  Director of Community Development Chuck Wilson presented the staff report.

City Council Minutes  4  March 7, 2011
   Michael Battaglia, Standard Pacific Homes, presented the proposal and discussed the
  benefits of annexation, both for the City of Mission Viejo and for the future homeowners
  of the Skyridge development. Mr. Battaglia answered questions of the City Council
  Members.

  Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: expressed support for the proposal.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to direct
  staff to fully confirm and identify parameters by which the annexation would go forward,
  a general outline of the process to be followed including a preliminary schedule and
  Council decision points, and return to the City Council with a report.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

14.  Oso Parkway Widening - I-5 to Country Club Drive (CIP 791)

  Celeste Brady, Special Counsel, Stradling Yocca Carlson & Rauth, presented the staff
  report and answered question of the City Council.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, to (1) adopt
  City Council Resolution No. 11-20 Approving a Cooperation and Public Improvements
  Agreement with the Community Development Agency of the City of Mission Viejo;
  Consenting to Payment by the Community Development Agency of All or a Part of the
  Cost of the Land Necessary for the Installation and Construction of Certain Oso Parkway
  Public Improvements; and Making Certain Findings in Connection Therewith; (2) adopt
  CDA Resolution 11-05 Approving a Cooperation and Public Improvements Agreement
  with the City of Mission Viejo; Committing Funds and Consenting to Payment by the
  Community Development Agency of All or a Part of the Cost of the Land Necessary for
  the Installation and Construction of Those Certain Oso Parkway Public Improvements;
  and Making Certain Findings in Connection Therewith and (3) adopt CDA Resolution
  11-06, Amending the FY 2010-11 Budget for costs related to the Oso Parkway Widening
  - I-5 to Country Club Drive Project.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

City Council Minutes  5  March 7, 2011
 15.  CDA Authorization to Transfer $5.7M from the Housing Fund to the Mission Viejo
  Housing Authority for Affordable Housing Purposes and Project(s)

  Celeste Brady, Special Counsel, Stradling Yocca Carlson & Rauth, presented the staff
  report and answered the City Council Member's questions.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, to authorize
  the CDA Executive Director and Director of Administrative Services to Transfer $5.7M
  from the CDA’s Housing Fund to the Mission Viejo Housing Authority for Affordable
  Housing Purposes and projects that Comply with the California Community
  Redevelopment Law, The California Housing Authorities Law and Other Applicable
  Laws and Regulations.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

RECESS

At the hour of 7:51 p.m., Mayor Leckness declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at
7:59 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

7.  Fiscal Year 2010 Urban Area Security Initiative Grant Programs for Emergency
  Preparedness

  Emergency Services Manager Paul Catsimanes presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, to (1)
  authorize the City Manager to execute a contract with the City of Anaheim entitled,
  "Agreement to Transfer or Purchase of Equipment/Services or for Reimbursement of
  Training Costs For FY Urban Area Security Initiative (UASI)" and (2) adopt Resolution
  11-14 Authorizing Certain Positions to Act as Agents to Execute Documents for
  Financial Assistance Provided by the Federal Department of Homeland Security and Sub-
  Granted Through the State of California.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

City Council Minutes  6  March 7, 2011
 8.  Regional Traffic Signal Synchronization Program (Project P) Applications for
  Measure M2 Competitive Funding

  Council Member Kelley stated that she removed this item from the Consent Calendar to
  highlight the fact that staff is being aggressive and proactive in trying to obtain funding
  for improvements that benefit the residents.

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the staff report and answered
  questions of the City Council.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to
  adopt Resolution 11-15 Approving the Submittal of the Crown Valley Parkway Corridor,
  the Marguerite Parkway Corridor, and the Irvine Road-Trabuco Road Corridor
  Improvement Projects to the Orange County Transportation Authority for Funding Under
  the Competitive Measure M2 Regional Transportation Signal Synchronization Program.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

9.  Animal License Amnesty Days

  Council Member Schlicht stated that there is a significant percentage of animal license
  delinquencies and she asked if there is a problem with the City's servicing agent.

  Director of Public Services Keith Rattay indicated that this is a sign of the economy and
  Mission Viejo actually has a lower percentage of delinquencies than most cities. He also
  reported that the staff processes animal licenses in-house and there is no outside servicing
  agent.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to
  adopt Resolution 11-16 Waiving Current Delinquent Animal License Fees Between the
  Period of April 1, 2011 and April 30, 2011 for the Purposes of Conducting Animal
  Licensing Amnesty Days in Mission Viejo.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

City Council Minutes  7  March 7, 2011
 10.  Crown Valley Parkway Widening (CIP 752)

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon provided an explanation of the history of the
  project and the funding sources.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, to (1)
  approve Contract Change Order 3 in the amount of $1,798,786 to All American Asphalt,
  Inc.; (2) certify the completion of and accept the improvements for the subject project;
  (3) authorize the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (4) authorize the City
  Clerk to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the
  faithful performance and payment bonds 35 days after the date of recordation of the
  Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed with the City; (5)
  authorize payment of the remaining construction contract retention; (6) authorize the
  issuance of a purchase order in the amount of $40,048 to RBF Consulting, Inc., for
  additional construction staking and construction support services; and (7) adopt
  Resolution 11-17 Amending the Fiscal Year 2010-2011 Budget for Costs Related to
  Capital Improvement Project 752.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

16.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Council Member Kelley stated that there has not been a recent meeting of the OCFA
  therefore she has nothing to report at this time.

17.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Ury presented the report.

18.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Leckness presented the report.

19.  SCAG Transportation & Communications Committee (TCC) Report

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

City Council Minutes  8  March 7, 2011
 20.  Appointment to the Planning & Transportation Commission

  Motion made by Council Member Reardon, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, to appoint
  Cliff Swan to the Planning and Transportation Commission.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

Council Member Schlicht inquired about the City's newsletter advertisement for chalk artists and
she asked if the city is hijacking Frank Lieberman's Fun With Chalk event.

City Manager Wilberg announced that the city is not doing a Fun With Chalk event but is
following the Council's direction to combine a chalk festival with Arts Alive. He noted that Dr.
Lieberman has some health issues and is unable to hold Fun With Chalk this year. The City is
hiring chalk artists with the help of Dr. Lieberman's Board Members and staff will do an
excellent job with the event, as they have done supporting Fun With Chalk in the past.

City Attorney's Report

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

21.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley outlined her attendance at the Orange County Community Association
conference on February 22 where participants received an economic and market conditions
update. She stated that it’s wonderful that resident Wendy Bucknum is President of that
Association. Council Member Kelley also discussed her attendance at the Viejo Little League
opening day on February 26 and she apologized for missing a few additional events when she
was out of town for a week. Council Member Kelley announced that the Community of
Character word for the month of March is integrity.

City Council Minutes  9  March 7, 2011
 Council Member Reardon

Council Member Reardon outlined her attendance at opening day for the South Mission Viejo
Little League. She enjoyed taking her grandsons and she was pleased to meet some really
wonderful residents that day. She also discussed the briefing that she attended with Peter
Bastone, CEO of Mission Hospital. It was an enlightening tour and she was very impressed and
appreciative of the time that Mr. Bastone gave her. Council Member Reardon announced that
she attended the Association of California Cities public policy seminar and it was extremely
interesting to hear the County’s CEO, Tom Mauk. Finally, she thanked staff, especially
Information Technology personnel, for helping her with some technical challenges.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht asked City Attorney Curley about developing parameters regarding
private enterprises installing donation boxes on public property.

Mr. Curley responded that he recommends her suggestion be embraced.

Council Member Schlicht commended the Rancho Santa Margarita City Council for re-thinking
the replacement of one of their Council Members who is away on military leave. She
appreciates that they are going to determine how they can keep him involved from afar via
teleconference or some other means. Council Member Schlicht announced that she too attended
the opening for the Viejo Little League and she stated that it’s the parents that make the
difference. She also enjoyed watching the Saddleback Gauchos win a recent basketball game
and she stated that her heart goes out to the Mission Viejo Diablos who lost a football game by
one point to Anaheim. She stated that it was victory in itself for the Diablos to be there. Council
Member Schlicht ended her comments with a quote from Craig R. Smith, “The idea that political
speech had to be protected at any cost dates to Colonial days, during which the press and the
public were not allowed to express themselves freely on matters of public concern. The King and
his government often used restrictive measures, such as licensing of printing presses and the
doctrine of seditious libel, to silence unfavorable public comment.”

Mayor Pro Tem Ury

Mayor Pro Tem Ury discussed recent meetings of the Association of California Cities, Orange
County (ACCOC). The guest speakers discussed a variety of topics including air quality issues,
housing, transportation, and pension reform.  He noted that here are three ACCOC
subcommittees and he will keep the Council informed of the pension reform subcommittee’s
work. Mayor Pro Tem Ury announced that he too had a great time at the South Mission Viejo
Little League opening day and he looks forward to attending many baseball games this year.

Mayor Leckness

Mayor Leckness announced that he gave a speech at the Little League opening day and he
created quite a few laughs when he, the Mayor, encouraged kids to “steal” bases. He also

City Council Minutes  10  March 7, 2011
 discussed his attendance at the KSBR event at the Murray Community Center with jazz artist
Earl Klugh. He noted that KSBR consistently provides top-notch programs and it was a fantastic
show. Mayor Leckness reminded his colleagues to present their position in a positive way.
Using negative language sends the wrong message and creates barriers. He stated that all five
Council Members need to watch the language that they use because ultimately, the goal is to get
things done for the City’s residents.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour or 9:20 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Leckness adjourned the meeting to Monday, March 21, 2011, at 5:00 p.m.

__________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of March 21, 2011

City Council Minutes  11  March 7, 2011
